question: What is the sum of all real numbers \(x\) for which the median of the numbers \(4,\) \(6,\) \(8,\) \(17,\) and \(x\) is equal to the mean of those five numbers?
solution:
The median is the third number after sorting, so its value changes according to where \(x\) lies relative to \(6\) and \(8\). The mean is
\[
\frac{4+6+8+17+x}{5}=\frac{x+35}{5}.
\]
Consider three disjoint cases that cover every real \(x\).

If \(x<6\), the median is \(6\). Equating mean and median gives
\[
\frac{x+35}{5}=6
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=-5,
\]
which satisfies \(x<6\).

If \(6\le x\le8\), the median is \(x\). Then
\[
\frac{x+35}{5}=x
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 35=4x
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=\frac{35}{4}.
\]
But \(35/4>8\), so this case gives no solution.

If \(x>8\), the median is \(8\). Then
\[
\frac{x+35}{5}=8
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=5,
\]
which fails \(x>8\).

Thus the only valid value is \(-5\), and the requested sum is \(\boxed{-5}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
